title: GitHub backend: repositories, members, invites, archive/unarchive, project files and the local project folder
summary: The GitHub store can create a private project repository or connect an existing (also empty) one, keep members and invitations, save sources, sessions, PRD structure, versions and scores under .grillo/ through a local clone, and archive or reopen a project; before this every repository store call was a stub.
friction: The dev agent ran a live check against real GitHub and left a private archived repository (grillo-throwaway-73) that the gh token cannot delete; a person must refresh the token scope and delete it
lessons_learned: Store backends can be proven with real git against a local bare repository behind a fake gh, as both later reviewers did; the dev brief should say so, so no live repository is ever created

Each review round on the GitHub store found a real data or access bug (staged leftovers breaking numbering, case-sensitive logins leaving admin invites open, unvalidated text fields, empty repositories refused); budget for more than one round on store stories

deferred.what: On a protected main every save returns a result planned from main without the change: two createSource calls both return S1 and open two pull requests adding the same file, and updateSession right after createSession (or setScore right after createPrdVersion) refuses not-found until someone merges
deferred.why: Needs a numbering design for unmerged saves (read pending grillo/save-* branches, or one long-lived save branch); the story followed the documented rule

deferred.what: The backend calls an optional onPullRequest when a save became a pull request, but nothing passes one in, so the member is not told and sees main unchanged
deferred.why: Needs a screen to show the notice

deferred.what: listProjects rejects as a whole when one recent project has a damaged Grillo file (backend) or a folder that cannot fast-forward (conflict), hiding every other project
deferred.why: Skipping quietly would hide a broken project and a signed-out gh is also a backend error; the project list screen must decide how to show it
